prompt: When is `viewModelScope` cancelled?
hint: It lives exactly as long as its owner.

choices.text: At every rotation of the phone
choices.why: A rotation keeps the ViewModel, so it keeps its scope too.

choices.text: When it is cleared, in `onCleared()`
choices.why: Right: `CancelTest` cleared the store and the write was cancelled.

choices.text: When the activity stops
choices.why: Stopping changes what the screen collects, not the ViewModel's scope.

choices.text: Never: it lives as long as the process
choices.why: That describes `GlobalScope`, which section 02 calls the wrong picture.

prompt: Why does `SlowStore` rethrow the `CancellationException` it catches?
hint: Cancellation is cooperative.

choices.text: Because Kotlin refuses to compile a catch that swallows it
choices.why: It compiles; swallowing it is a bug the compiler does not see.

choices.text: So the coroutine really stops
choices.why: Right: a coroutine that swallows it carries on as if nothing had been asked.

choices.text: So the test prints `write completed` afterwards
choices.why: The rethrow is exactly what stops `write completed` from ever printing.

choices.text: Because `delay` needs it to restart
choices.why: A cancelled `delay` does not restart.

prompt: The student presses **Add** and closes the app at once. Why might `viewModelScope` be the wrong place for that write?
hint: What happens to the scope when the screen goes for good?

choices.text: An unfinished write dies with the ViewModel
choices.why: Right: work that must outlive the screen goes to WorkManager, lesson 18.

choices.text: `viewModelScope` runs on a background thread that is too slow
choices.why: It runs on `Main`; speed is not the issue, lifetime is.

choices.text: The write would run twice, once per activity
choices.why: One ViewModel launches it once, whatever the activities do.

choices.text: Closing the app keeps the scope alive for an hour
choices.why: Closing clears the ViewModel and cancels the scope.

prompt: Why is `initialValue` set to `WeekUiState(loading = true)` instead of an empty list?
hint: What would an empty list say to the student?

choices.text: An empty list would be a false claim
choices.why: Right: loading is the honest first state.

choices.text: `stateIn` refuses an empty list
choices.why: It accepts any value of the type.

choices.text: A loading state makes `combine` run faster
choices.why: The initial value has no effect on speed.

choices.text: Because `SavedStateHandle` needs a boolean
choices.why: The handle holds the draft; `loading` is not in it.

prompt: Match each `started` policy to when the store is collected.
hint: The table in section 03.

pairs.right: From the ViewModel's creation to its end
From the first collector to the ViewModel's end
While collected, and five seconds after

right_distractors: Only while the activity is resumed

prompt: After this lesson's rewrite, how does a new session reach `state` once `onAdd` runs?
hint: No function builds the state by hand any more.

choices.text: `onAdd` calls `_state.update` with the new list
choices.why: That was lesson 10; there is no `_state` now.

choices.text: The store emits, and `combine` follows
choices.why: Right: one path for every change, whoever made it.

choices.text: The screen adds it to its own copy of the list
choices.why: The screen holds no copy; that is lesson 10's one-way flow.

choices.text: The channel delivers it to the state
choices.why: The channel carries the snackbar event, not the session.

prompt: `saved.___(DRAFT, "")` turns a key of the `SavedStateHandle` into a `StateFlow`.
hint: Its name says what it returns.

prompt: In `SubscriptionTest`, how many collectors did the store have four seconds after the activity stopped?
hint: The grace period is five seconds.

prompt: What does `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()` do that `collectAsState()` does not?
hint: Press the home button.

choices.text: It stops collecting below `STARTED`
choices.why: Right: `collectAsState` collects while the composable is composed, stopped or not.

choices.text: It keeps the last value across process death
choices.why: Neither survives the process; that is `SavedStateHandle`'s job.

choices.text: It collects on a background thread
choices.why: Both collect on the main thread for the composition.

choices.text: It converts a cold flow into a hot one
choices.why: That is `stateIn`, in the ViewModel.

prompt: Someone changes `WhileSubscribed(5_000)` to `WhileSubscribed(0)`. What changes at each rotation?
hint: During a rotation, for a moment, nobody collects.

choices.text: Nothing, because the ViewModel survives the rotation
choices.why: The ViewModel survives, but its upstream stops the instant the last collector leaves.

choices.text: The upstream restarts each time
choices.why: Right: the grace period is what lets a rotation pass without that.

choices.text: The screen keeps collecting in the background
choices.why: Background collection is decided by `collectAsStateWithLifecycle`, unchanged here.

choices.text: The state is lost and shows loading for good
choices.why: It restarts with the new collector and loads again.

prompt: Why must a composable not call `viewModel.events.collect` directly in its body?
hint: How often does a body run?

choices.text: The body reruns at each recomposition, restarting it
choices.why: Right: work starts in `LaunchedEffect` or from a callback.

choices.text: Because `collect` is not allowed on a `Flow` of events
choices.why: It is allowed; the question is where.

choices.text: Because events must be collected in the activity
choices.why: The route collects them, in a `LaunchedEffect`.

choices.text: Because the snackbar cannot be shown from Compose
choices.why: The planner shows it from Compose through `SnackbarHostState`.

prompt: The total's tap shows "That is 2 h 40 min" in a snackbar. Why is it launched with `rememberCoroutineScope` and not `LaunchedEffect`?
hint: Who decides when it starts?

choices.text: Because `LaunchedEffect` cannot call `showSnackbar`
choices.why: It can, and the event collector does exactly that.

choices.text: A tap starts it: a callback, not being on screen
choices.why: Right: a callback launches into the remembered scope.

choices.text: Because the ViewModel must not know about hours
choices.why: True that the screen does the conversion, but that is not why the scope differs.

choices.text: Because `rememberCoroutineScope` survives rotation
choices.why: It is cancelled when the composable leaves the composition.

prompt: Put the life of the `LaunchedEffect(viewModel)` in `WeekRoute` in order.
hint: It belongs to being on screen.
items: an `Added` event arrives and a snackbar is shown
`WeekRoute` leaves the composition and the coroutine is cancelled

prompt: If "Added 45 min" were a `message` field in `WeekUiState`, what would happen at the next rotation?
hint: The new screen reads the state from the start.

choices.text: Nothing, rotation does not touch the state
choices.why: Exactly: the state is kept, message included, and the new screen draws it.

choices.text: The snackbar would appear again
choices.why: Right, unless the screen reports it shown and the ViewModel clears it.

choices.text: The message would be lost
choices.why: State survives a rotation; the problem is showing it twice.

choices.text: The app would refuse to compile
choices.why: It compiles; the bug is in behaviour.

prompt: Why does the planner use `Channel(Channel.BUFFERED)` rather than a `MutableSharedFlow` with no replay for its events?
hint: What happens to an event sent while nobody listens?

choices.text: A channel is faster for small objects
choices.why: Speed is not the argument; delivery is.

choices.text: A shared flow cannot carry a sealed interface
choices.why: It can carry any type.

choices.text: The channel keeps the event until a receiver comes
choices.why: Right: during a rotation there is briefly no collector, and the shared flow would drop it.

choices.text: Only a channel can be collected in `LaunchedEffect`
choices.why: Any flow can be collected there.

prompt: A save fails and the student must see why before trying again. Following this lesson, where does that error go?
hint: Messages that are only information take one path; this is not one of them.

choices.text: Into the channel, like "Added 45 min"
choices.why: The channel can lose an event in a narrow case, which is acceptable only for information.

choices.text: Into the UI state, until it has been seen
choices.why: Right: what must be seen goes in the state, as Google's guide argues.

choices.text: Into a log, since the screen cannot show errors
choices.why: The screen can show anything the state carries.

choices.text: Into the `SavedStateHandle` alone
choices.why: The handle is for surviving the process, not for showing things.

prompt: Why do this lesson's ViewModel tests call `Dispatchers.setMain`?
hint: Which dispatcher does `viewModelScope` use?

choices.text: The JVM has no Android main looper
choices.why: Right: `viewModelScope` runs on `Main`, which the test replaces with a test dispatcher.

choices.text: To make the tests run on several threads at once
choices.why: A test dispatcher runs on one thread, in virtual time.

choices.text: Because `runTest` refuses to start without it
choices.why: `runTest` starts fine; `onAdd` is what would fail.

choices.text: To get Robolectric's looper
choices.why: These tests use no Robolectric at all.

prompt: In `withNobodyCollectingTheStateStaysLoading`, a session is added and `state.value.loading` is still true. Why?
hint: What starts the upstream?

choices.text: The write was cancelled
choices.why: Nothing cancelled it; the store has the session.

choices.text: `UnconfinedTestDispatcher` never runs `launch`
choices.why: It runs them at once; the store was written.

choices.text: Nobody collected `state`, so `WhileSubscribed` never started the upstream
choices.why: Right: the second test starts a collector in `backgroundScope` first.

choices.text: `loading` can only become false on a device
choices.why: The second test turned it false on the JVM.

prompt: How many tests did the whole run of this lesson execute, across its four test classes?
hint: Add the `tests=` of each suite.

prompt: A collector started in `runTest`'s `___` is cancelled by itself when the test ends.
hint: Section 07's second test.

prompt: Which of these start a coroutine in a place this lesson approves? Choose all that apply.
hint: Scope of the ViewModel, an effect, or a callback.

choices.text: `viewModelScope.launch { store.add(…) }` in `onAdd`
choices.why: Yes: it ends with the ViewModel.

choices.text: `GlobalScope.launch` in a button's `onClick`
choices.why: No: it outlives the screen and anything it belonged to.

choices.text: `LaunchedEffect(viewModel) { viewModel.events.collect { … } }`
choices.why: Yes: it starts and ends with the composable.

choices.text: `runBlocking { store.add(…) }` in a composable's body
choices.why: No: it blocks the main thread at every recomposition.

prompt: A screen shows live data from a network flow. The student opens another app for two minutes. With this lesson's setup, what is the network doing during those two minutes?
hint: Two mechanisms, five seconds.

choices.text: Idle, after the first five seconds
choices.why: Right: `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` stops at once and `WhileSubscribed(5_000)` five seconds later.

choices.text: Still fetching, because the ViewModel is alive
choices.why: Being alive does not mean collecting; `WhileSubscribed` stops the upstream.

choices.text: Fetching for two minutes and then stopping
choices.why: The grace period is five seconds, not the time away.

choices.text: Nothing, because the process is always killed
choices.why: The process may well survive two minutes; the lifecycle is what stops the work.
